title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. S/T is a scheme over T. E is an O_S-module with a stratification δ = δ^∞_E. P^∞_{S/T}(E) is the module of principal parts (infinite jets) of E, and P^∞(E)^+ is its augmentation-ideal part. P is a torsor under E. On the previous page Grothendieck showed the following. Stratifications on P compatible with δ correspond to maps λ: P → P^∞(E)/δE, equivalently λ^+: P → P^∞(E)^+, satisfying conditions (27), (28) and (31). Reducing λ^+ to first order through P^1(E)^+ ≅ E⊗Ω^1 gives a map d_P: P → E⊗Ω^1 with d_P(x+ξ) = d_P(x) + d_E(ξ). This map is the connection on P, it is integrable, and its class in H^1_DR(S,E) is the image of the class of (P,λ) in H^1_Strat(S,E) under the canonical map (24).

Corollary (top of this page). Assume char T = 0 and Ω^1_{S/T} flat, e.g. S formally smooth, so that (24) is an isomorphism. Then the following are in bijection:
- compatible stratifications on P;
- compatible integrable connections on P;
- maps λ^+ satisfying (27), (28), (31);
- homomorphisms d_P satisfying (18).
The bijection sends λ^+ to its reduction in P^1(E)^+ ≅ E⊗Ω^1.

NB. Apply this to the trivial torsor P = E. Integrable compatible connections on it are given by ∇-closed E-valued 1-forms. Grothendieck concludes that the truncation P^∞(E)^+ → P^1(E)^+ restricts to a sheaf isomorphism P^∞(E)^{+δ} ≅ Z^1(E⊗Ω^1_{S/T}).
- The δ-invariants are taken for a 'second' stratification on P^∞(E)^+. It is transported, via (29), from the canonical stratification of P^∞(E)/δE.
- So every closed 1-form with coefficients in E integrates uniquely to a horizontal infinite jet λ^+ satisfying (28).
- An exact form d_E(ξ) corresponds to λ^+(ξ) = d^∞_E(ξ) − δ^∞_E(ξ), the 'difference of the two stratifications'.
In modern terms this is a sheafified formal Poincaré lemma in degree 1. It is also the jet/crystalline interpretation of H^1_DR(S,E) as stratified E-torsors, i.e. extensions of O by E in the category of crystals.

Section 4, 'Équations de Picard–Fuchs'. E is again stratified, with δ^∞_E = δ. Grothendieck takes an exact sequence (33) 0 → E' → E → E'' → 0 of modules in which E' is NOT assumed to be a stratified submodule; it is a Hodge-type filtration step. He begins 'Supposons donné un …' and the page breaks off; the next sheet is blank. The evident goal is the Kodaira–Spencer / second-fundamental-form map E' → E''⊗Ω^1. From it one gets the differential equations satisfied by the periods (sections of E' paired with horizontal sections), i.e. Picard–Fuchs equations seen through the Gauss–Manin connection and the Hodge filtration.
errors:
No mathematical error is visible. Two implicit points:
- Z^1 must be read as the kernel of ∇^1: E⊗Ω^1 → E⊗Ω^2 (∇-closed forms), not as closed forms in a naive sense.
- The isomorphism uses char 0 (formal Poincaré lemma) and flatness of Ω^1. In characteristic p it fails, because closed forms need not lift to horizontal ∞-jets (divided powers are needed).
Notation is loose. The page writes d^0_E(ξ) for what is d^1-type data (the exact form ∇ξ), and the final expression 'd^+_E(ξ)^+' is garbled shorthand for d^∞_E(ξ) − δ^∞_E(ξ).

ideas.what: Correspondence between compatible stratifications on an E-torsor and integrable connections on it (char 0, Ω^1 flat), via reduction of infinite jets to first order.
ideas.modern_name: Equivalence of stratifications/crystals and integrable connections in char 0; torsor description of H^1_dR = H^1_crys
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes, 1966/68); Berthelot (1974)
ideas.where_published: 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968); EGA IV 16 for principal parts

ideas.what: Isomorphism of sheaves P^∞(E)^{+δ} ≅ Z^1(E⊗Ω^1): every ∇-closed 1-form integrates uniquely to a horizontal infinite jet.
ideas.modern_name: Formal Poincaré lemma / linearization of the de Rham complex (degree 1)
ideas.where_published: Close to the linearization arguments in 'Crystals and de Rham cohomology' (1968) and in Berthelot's thesis

ideas.what: Setup for Picard–Fuchs equations: stratified E with a submodule E' that is not stratified (a filtration step).
ideas.modern_name: Gauss–Manin connection with Hodge filtration; Kodaira–Spencer map / second fundamental form; Griffiths transversality
ideas.where_published: Not in Grothendieck's published texts as far as known; the Gauss–Manin connection is the topic of Katz–Oda

missed.claim: The section 'Équations de Picard–Fuchs' is only begun: a stratified E with a non-stratified submodule E', with the definition cut off ('Supposons donné un'). The intended treatment of Picard–Fuchs via stratifications and torsors is therefore not on this page. Its likely content (second fundamental form, cyclic vectors) is standard today through Griffiths and Katz.
missed.quote: On ne suppose pas que E' soit un sous-module stratifié. Supposons donné un
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of mainly historical interest. It shows Grothendieck framing Picard–Fuchs inside the jet/stratification (crystalline) language around 1972. This may be relevant to char-p or p-adic versions, where stratifications and connections differ.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but standard development: stratified torsors, integrable connections, and the formal Poincaré lemma in degree 1. All of it is known from Grothendieck's crystals paper and Berthelot. The Picard–Fuchs section stops at the setup.
transcription_corrections: The displayed exact sequence is numbered '(33)', not '(30)'. Equation (32) already appears on the previous page, and the handwriting reads (33).
In 'jet d'ordre ∞ λ^+ de E sur S/T', the words 'de' and 'sur' appear underlined or overwritten rather than deleted. The intended phrase is roughly '[définit un] jet d'ordre ∞ λ^+ de E sur S/T'.
'une suite exacte de modules [?] p. ex.' — the illegible word may be 'quasi-coh.' or similar; uncertain.
